meta.subject: science
meta.description: Earth science facts: layers of earth, plate tectonics, rock cycle, water cycle, weather, natural resources, soil, erosion, atmosphere

facts.statement: The Earth has four main layers: crust, mantle, outer core, and inner core
The crust is the thinnest outer layer, ranging from 5 km (oceanic) to 70 km (continental) thick
The mantle is the thickest layer, about 2,900 km thick, made of semi-solid rock that can flow slowly
The outer core is liquid iron and nickel, about 2,200 km thick, and generates Earth's magnetic field
The inner core is solid iron and nickel, about 1,200 km in radius, kept solid by extreme pressure despite extreme heat
The lithosphere (crust + upper mantle) is rigid and broken into tectonic plates
The asthenosphere is the partially molten layer of the upper mantle beneath the lithosphere; tectonic plates float on it
The Mohorovicic discontinuity (Moho) is the boundary between the crust and the mantle, detected by changes in seismic wave speed
Earth's layers increase in temperature and pressure with depth; the inner core reaches about 5,400 degrees Celsius
Earth's magnetic field is generated by convection currents of liquid iron in the outer core (the geodynamo)
Seismic waves from earthquakes travel at different speeds through different materials, allowing scientists to map Earth's interior
P-waves (primary waves) travel through both solids and liquids; S-waves (secondary waves) only travel through solids
The shadow zone caused by the outer core's liquid state is evidence that the outer core is liquid (S-waves cannot pass through)
Oceanic crust is denser than continental crust because it is made primarily of basalt, while continental crust is primarily granite
Convection currents in the mantle are driven by heat from the core and radioactive decay, causing slow circulation of mantle material
Earth is approximately 4.54 billion years old, determined by radiometric dating of the oldest rocks and meteorites

common_errors.wrong: the center of Earth is hollow
common_errors.correct: The center of Earth contains a solid inner core of iron and nickel at extremely high temperature and pressure.

common_errors.wrong: the mantle is entirely liquid
common_errors.correct: Most of the mantle is solid but can flow very slowly over geological time. Only parts of the asthenosphere are partially molten.

common_errors.wrong: the crust is the same thickness everywhere
common_errors.correct: Oceanic crust (~5-10 km) is much thinner than continental crust (~30-70 km).

common_errors.wrong: we have drilled to the center of the Earth
common_errors.correct: The deepest drill hole (Kola Superdeep Borehole) reached only 12.2 km deep, barely scratching the crust. We know about deeper layers from seismic waves.

common_errors.wrong: the Earth's core is made of the same material as the crust
common_errors.correct: The core is mostly iron and nickel, while the crust is silicate rocks (granite and basalt). Density increases toward the center.

common_errors.wrong: the inner core is liquid because it is so hot
common_errors.correct: Despite extreme heat (~5,400 degrees C), the inner core is solid because the immense pressure prevents the iron from melting.

facts.statement: Tectonic plates are large pieces of Earth's lithosphere that float on the semi-fluid asthenosphere and move slowly over time
There are three types of plate boundaries: convergent (plates collide), divergent (plates separate), and transform (plates slide past each other)
Most earthquakes and volcanic eruptions occur along tectonic plate boundaries, especially around the Pacific Ring of Fire
Subduction occurs at convergent boundaries when one plate slides beneath another into the mantle
Continental drift is the theory, proposed by Alfred Wegener, that continents move over time; all continents were once joined as Pangaea
Mid-ocean ridges form at divergent boundaries where new oceanic crust is created by rising magma
The Ring of Fire is a horseshoe-shaped zone around the Pacific Ocean where about 75% of the world's volcanoes and 90% of earthquakes occur
Seafloor spreading occurs at mid-ocean ridges where magma rises, cools, and pushes older crust apart
Evidence for continental drift includes matching fossils, rock types, and mountain ranges on separate continents, plus the jigsaw-puzzle fit of coastlines
The San Andreas Fault in California is a transform boundary where the Pacific Plate slides past the North American Plate
Ocean trenches form at convergent boundaries where oceanic crust subducts; the Mariana Trench is the deepest at about 11,000 meters
Mountain ranges like the Himalayas form at convergent boundaries where two continental plates collide and push crust upward
Earthquakes are measured on the Richter scale (magnitude) and detected by seismographs; each whole number increase is 10x more ground motion
The epicenter is the point on Earth's surface directly above the earthquake's focus (hypocenter), where the rupture begins underground
Tectonic plates move at rates of 1 to 15 cm per year, roughly the speed at which fingernails grow
Volcanic islands like Hawaii form over hot spots, stationary plumes of magma rising from deep in the mantle, not at plate boundaries
Pangaea existed about 335-175 million years ago and began breaking apart during the Jurassic period
When oceanic crust meets continental crust at a convergent boundary, the denser oceanic crust always subducts beneath the lighter continental crust

common_errors.wrong: earthquakes can only happen along plate boundaries
common_errors.correct: While most earthquakes occur at plate boundaries, intraplate earthquakes can happen within plates due to old fault lines and stress accumulation.

common_errors.wrong: all volcanoes are at plate boundaries
common_errors.correct: Some volcanoes, like those in Hawaii, form over hot spots in the middle of tectonic plates, not at boundaries.

common_errors.wrong: Pangaea broke apart suddenly
common_errors.correct: Pangaea began breaking apart about 200 million years ago and the continents have been slowly moving apart since then.

common_errors.wrong: the continents are still in the same positions they have always been
common_errors.correct: The continents continue to move today. The Atlantic Ocean is widening by about 2.5 cm per year.

common_errors.wrong: earthquakes only happen in California
common_errors.correct: Earthquakes happen worldwide along plate boundaries and fault lines. The New Madrid Seismic Zone in central US has caused major earthquakes.

common_errors.wrong: an earthquake measuring 8 on the Richter scale is twice as strong as one measuring 4
common_errors.correct: Each whole number on the Richter scale represents 10x more ground motion and about 31.6x more energy. An 8 is 10,000x more ground motion than a 4.

facts.statement: The three main types of rocks are igneous (from cooled magma/lava), sedimentary (from compressed sediments), and metamorphic (changed by heat and pressure)
The rock cycle describes how rocks continuously change from one type to another over geological time
Igneous rocks form when magma (underground) or lava (above ground) cools and solidifies
Sedimentary rocks form when small pieces of rock, minerals, or organic material are deposited and cemented together over time
Metamorphic rocks form when existing rocks are changed by extreme heat and/or pressure without fully melting
Weathering breaks rocks into smaller pieces; erosion transports those pieces by wind, water, ice, or gravity
Fossils are found almost exclusively in sedimentary rocks because igneous and metamorphic processes destroy organic remains
Intrusive igneous rocks (like granite) cool slowly underground and have large visible crystals; extrusive igneous rocks (like basalt) cool quickly on the surface and have small crystals
Mechanical (physical) weathering breaks rocks without changing their chemical composition (frost wedging, root growth, abrasion)
Chemical weathering changes the chemical composition of rocks (acid rain dissolving limestone, oxidation of iron-bearing rocks)
Limestone (sedimentary) becomes marble (metamorphic) under heat and pressure; shale becomes slate
Minerals are naturally occurring, inorganic solids with a definite chemical composition and crystal structure; rocks are made of one or more minerals
The Mohs hardness scale rates minerals from 1 (talc, softest) to 10 (diamond, hardest)
Sedimentary rocks often form in layers called strata; lower layers are generally older (law of superposition)
Obsidian is an extrusive igneous rock that cools so rapidly it forms glass rather than crystals
Conglomerate, sandstone, and shale are sedimentary rocks classified by particle size (largest to smallest)
Deposition occurs when eroded material settles in a new location, often in layers at the bottom of bodies of water
Coal is a sedimentary rock formed from the remains of ancient plants compressed over millions of years
Geologic time is divided into eons, eras, periods, and epochs; we live in the Cenozoic Era, Quaternary Period, Holocene Epoch

common_errors.wrong: magma and lava are the same thing
common_errors.correct: Magma is molten rock below Earth's surface. Once it reaches the surface through a volcano, it is called lava.

common_errors.wrong: rocks cannot change from one type to another
common_errors.correct: The rock cycle shows that any rock type can be transformed into any other type through natural processes over geological time.

common_errors.wrong: fossils are found in all types of rocks
common_errors.correct: Fossils are found almost exclusively in sedimentary rocks. Heat and pressure from igneous and metamorphic processes typically destroy fossils.

common_errors.wrong: all rocks are millions of years old
common_errors.correct: Igneous rocks from recent volcanic eruptions can be days old. Lava that cools today becomes a new igneous rock immediately.

common_errors.wrong: erosion and weathering are the same thing
common_errors.correct: Weathering breaks rocks down in place. Erosion involves the transport of the broken pieces by wind, water, ice, or gravity.

common_errors.wrong: metamorphic rocks must melt to form
common_errors.correct: Metamorphic rocks form when existing rocks change due to heat and pressure WITHOUT melting. If rock melts, it becomes magma, which forms igneous rock when cooled.

facts.statement: The water cycle is the continuous movement of water through evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection
Evaporation is the process by which liquid water changes to water vapor (gas) when heated
Condensation is when water vapor cools and changes back into liquid water, forming clouds and fog
Precipitation occurs when water droplets in clouds become heavy enough to fall as rain, snow, sleet, or hail
Transpiration is the release of water vapor from plants through their leaves
About 97% of Earth's water is saltwater in the oceans; only about 3% is freshwater
Groundwater is water stored underground in spaces between rocks and soil, in formations called aquifers
Infiltration is the process by which water on the surface seeps into the ground through soil and rock
Runoff is water that flows over the ground surface into streams, rivers, and eventually the ocean
A watershed is an area of land where all water drains to a common outlet, such as a river or lake
About 69% of Earth's freshwater is locked in glaciers and ice caps; about 30% is groundwater; less than 1% is in surface water (rivers, lakes)
The water table is the upper boundary of the zone where rock and soil are saturated with groundwater
The total amount of water on Earth remains essentially constant; the water cycle has been recycling the same water for billions of years
Glaciers store freshwater as ice and release it slowly through melting; they shaped much of Earth's landscape during ice ages
The Sun provides the energy that drives the water cycle by heating water and causing evaporation

common_errors.wrong: the water cycle creates new water
common_errors.correct: The water cycle recycles the same water. No new water is created; it just changes states and locations.

common_errors.wrong: clouds are made of water vapor
common_errors.correct: Clouds are made of tiny liquid water droplets or ice crystals, not water vapor. Water vapor is invisible gas.

common_errors.wrong: most fresh water is in rivers and lakes
common_errors.correct: Most freshwater (about 69%) is locked in glaciers and ice caps. Groundwater accounts for about 30%. Rivers and lakes hold less than 1%.

common_errors.wrong: rain comes from the ocean only
common_errors.correct: Evaporation occurs from all water surfaces (lakes, rivers, soil, even puddles) and from transpiration by plants. The ocean is the largest source but not the only one.

common_errors.wrong: groundwater flows like underground rivers
common_errors.correct: Most groundwater moves very slowly through tiny spaces in rock and sediment (typically inches to feet per day), not as flowing rivers.

facts.statement: Weather is the short-term atmospheric conditions at a specific place; climate is the long-term average of weather patterns in a region
A cold front occurs when a mass of cold air pushes under warm air, often causing thunderstorms and a drop in temperature
A warm front occurs when warm air slides over cold air, often bringing clouds, rain, and gradual warming
Hurricanes (or typhoons/cyclones) form over warm ocean water and require sea surface temperatures of at least 26.5 degrees Celsius (80 degrees Fahrenheit)
Tornadoes are rotating columns of air that extend from thunderstorms to the ground, measured on the Enhanced Fujita (EF) Scale from EF0 to EF5
Air pressure decreases with increasing altitude because there is less atmosphere above pushing down
The atmosphere has five main layers: troposphere (weather occurs here), stratosphere (ozone layer), mesosphere, thermosphere, and exosphere
The troposphere is the lowest layer of the atmosphere (0-12 km), where all weather occurs and where we live
The ozone layer in the stratosphere absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation
A barometer measures atmospheric pressure; falling pressure often indicates approaching storms, rising pressure indicates fair weather
Humidity is the amount of water vapor in the air; relative humidity is the percentage of moisture the air holds compared to its maximum capacity at that temperature
Wind is caused by differences in air pressure: air flows from areas of high pressure to areas of low pressure
The Coriolis effect, caused by Earth's rotation, deflects moving air to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere
Jet streams are fast-flowing, narrow air currents in the upper atmosphere that influence weather patterns and storm tracks
El Nino is a periodic warming of the central and eastern Pacific Ocean that causes global weather disruptions
The three main climate zones are tropical (near equator, warm year-round), temperate (moderate, four seasons), and polar (cold, near poles)
Thunder is the sound caused by the rapid expansion of air heated by lightning, which reaches temperatures of about 30,000 K
Sea and land breezes occur because land heats and cools faster than water: land breeze at night (land to sea), sea breeze during day (sea to land)

common_errors.wrong: weather and climate are the same thing
common_errors.correct: Weather describes short-term conditions (today's rain). Climate describes long-term patterns (average rainfall over decades).

common_errors.wrong: lightning never strikes the same place twice
common_errors.correct: Lightning can and frequently does strike the same place multiple times. Tall structures like the Empire State Building are struck many times per year.

common_errors.wrong: the equator has the most seasons
common_errors.correct: Areas near the equator have the least seasonal variation. Seasons are most pronounced at temperate latitudes due to Earth's axial tilt.

common_errors.wrong: tornadoes only happen in Tornado Alley in the US
common_errors.correct: Tornadoes occur on every continent except Antarctica. While the US has the most, they happen worldwide.

common_errors.wrong: a cold day in winter disproves climate change
common_errors.correct: Weather is day-to-day variation. Climate change refers to long-term trends over decades. A single cold day is weather, not climate.

common_errors.wrong: the ozone hole caused global warming
common_errors.correct: The ozone hole (caused by CFCs) and global warming (caused by greenhouse gases like CO2) are separate environmental problems with different causes.

facts.statement: Renewable resources can be replenished naturally in a short time (solar energy, wind, water, trees); nonrenewable resources take millions of years to form (fossil fuels, minerals)
Fossil fuels (coal, oil, natural gas) formed from the remains of ancient organisms buried and compressed over millions of years
Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide (CO2), a greenhouse gas that traps heat in the atmosphere and contributes to global warming
The greenhouse effect is a natural process where certain gases in the atmosphere trap heat; without it, Earth would be about 33 degrees Celsius colder
Solar energy from the Sun can be converted to electricity using photovoltaic cells or used to heat water directly
Wind turbines convert kinetic energy of moving air into electricity; wind is caused by uneven heating of Earth's surface
Hydroelectric power generates electricity by using flowing water to turn turbines, often at dams
Geothermal energy harnesses heat from Earth's interior; it is most accessible near tectonic plate boundaries and volcanic areas
Soil is a nonrenewable resource on human timescales: it takes about 500 years to form 1 inch of topsoil
The three Rs of conservation are Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, listed in order of environmental impact (reducing is most effective)
Earth's average surface temperature has risen about 1.1 degrees Celsius since pre-industrial times, primarily due to increased greenhouse gas emissions
Nuclear energy produces no direct carbon emissions but creates radioactive waste that must be safely stored for thousands of years

common_errors.wrong: the greenhouse effect is entirely bad
common_errors.correct: The natural greenhouse effect is essential for life on Earth. Without it, Earth would be too cold for life. The problem is the enhanced greenhouse effect from extra CO2.

common_errors.wrong: renewable energy has no environmental impact
common_errors.correct: While cleaner than fossil fuels, renewable energy has impacts: dams alter rivers, wind turbines affect birds, solar farms use land. The impacts are much smaller though.

common_errors.wrong: we will never run out of fossil fuels
common_errors.correct: Fossil fuels are finite and nonrenewable. Known oil and gas reserves are estimated to last decades to a century at current consumption rates.

common_errors.wrong: recycling alone can solve the waste problem
common_errors.correct: Reducing consumption is more effective than recycling. Many materials can only be recycled a limited number of times before degrading.

common_errors.wrong: global warming means every place gets warmer equally
common_errors.correct: Climate change causes varied effects: some areas get warmer, some get more extreme weather, some get more precipitation, and ocean currents may shift.

facts.statement: Soil is a mixture of weathered rock particles, organic matter (humus), water, air, and living organisms
A soil profile has layers called horizons: O (organic), A (topsoil), B (subsoil), C (weathered parent rock), R (bedrock)
Topsoil (A horizon) is the most fertile layer, rich in organic matter and nutrients where most plant roots grow
Humus is the dark, organic material in soil formed from decomposed plants and animals; it improves soil fertility and water retention
The three main soil particle sizes are sand (largest, 0.05-2 mm), silt (medium, 0.002-0.05 mm), and clay (smallest, less than 0.002 mm)
Loam is the ideal soil for farming, containing roughly equal parts sand, silt, and clay with organic matter
Soil formation depends on five factors: parent material, climate, organisms, topography, and time
Earthworms improve soil by aerating it (creating tunnels), mixing organic matter, and producing nutrient-rich castings
Soil erosion by wind and water removes topsoil; farming practices like terracing, cover cropping, and contour plowing help prevent it
Clay soil holds water well but drains poorly; sandy soil drains quickly but holds little water and nutrients

common_errors.wrong: soil is just dirt with no life in it
common_errors.correct: Healthy soil teems with life: bacteria, fungi, earthworms, insects, and other organisms. A single teaspoon of soil can contain billions of microorganisms.

common_errors.wrong: all soil is the same everywhere
common_errors.correct: Soil varies enormously based on climate, parent rock, organisms, topography, and age. Desert soil is very different from forest soil or prairie soil.

common_errors.wrong: soil can be replaced quickly if eroded
common_errors.correct: It takes about 500 years to form just 1 inch of topsoil naturally. Erosion can remove topsoil far faster than it forms.

common_errors.wrong: sand is the best soil for growing plants
common_errors.correct: Sandy soil drains too quickly and holds few nutrients. Loam (a mix of sand, silt, clay, and organic matter) is best for most plants.
